correctness.rationale: The formula for the numerical index is a verified published theorem, not conjectural. Substitution t=exp(-2z/p) yields the claimed hyperbolic profile for every real exponent and both conjugate ranges. Its derivative has a single root because tanh(eta*z)tanh(z) rises strictly from 0 to 1. Strict monotonicity/convexity and the smooth-end Taylor law follow from exact pointwise/implicit calculus. At the polyhedral endpoint, the critical equation is exactly eps=2(u+v)/[(1+u)(1+v)], with u=e^(-2z), v=u^(1-eps). Uniform first estimates imply u,v are order eps, eps*z tends to zero, and Taylor expansion yields u=eps/4[1+eps(1-L)/2+O(eps^2 L^2)] and the paired v expression. Taking logs of the exact maximized value proves the eps and eps^2 log terms. Numerical finite checks pass but are not used as proof.

Full primary-text comparisons of the 2009 scalar formula, the 2022 partial-exponent proof, and the 2026 all-exponent theorem found no sharp two-term logarithmic endpoint deficit or first correction to the moving maximizer. The derived nonanalytic eps*log(1/eps) deficit, its explicit second correction, and logarithmic drift of the unique extremizer provide precise boundary geometry, not an arbitrary slice or standalone numerical table entry.
